details:
* SECURITY UPDATE: predictable TCP initial sequence numbers
     - debian/patches/CVE-2023-45236.patch: derive TCP initial sequence
       numbers from a SHA-256 hash of the connection addresses and ports and
       a per-boot random secret in NetworkPkg/TcpDxe, and add Hash2DxeCrypto
       to the OVMF, AAVMF and AAVMF32 images.
     - CVE-2023-45236
   * SECURITY UPDATE: weak pseudo-random number generator in the network stack
     - debian/patches/CVE-2023-45237.patch: replace NET_RANDOM() and
       NetRandomInitSeed() with PseudoRandom() backed by EFI_RNG_PROTOCOL in
       NetworkPkg, add a CPUID check and RDRAND self-test to BaseRngLib,
       install EFI_RNG_PROTOCOL from RngDxe only when RDRAND works, add RngDxe
       to OVMF, and re-run the DXE dispatcher after connecting virtio-rng in
       OVMF, AAVMF and AAVMF32.
       Network boot now requires an RNG source: OVMF (x86_64) needs an
       RDRAND-capable vCPU or a virtio-rng device; AAVMF and AAVMF32 need
       a virtio-rng device.
     - CVE-2023-45237
   * SECURITY UPDATE: PXE ICMP error buffer overflow
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-97631.patch: clear the ICMP error buffer,
       truncate ICMP/ICMPv6 error fragments at the end of the 504-byte
       buffer and advance the copy destination by each fragment's length in
       NetworkPkg/UefiPxeBcDxe/PxeBcSupport.c.
     - CVE-2026-97631
   * debian/control, debian/rules: build-depend on gcc-x86-64-linux-gnu on
     arm64 and use it to cross-build the OVMF (x86_64) firmware there, so
     the arch-independent packages also build on arm64 hosts.
